significance.quote: These constraints show a (full-space) parameter difference of 1.8$\sigma$ from a combination of cosmic microwave background (CMB) primary anisotropy datasets from Planck 2018, ACT-DR6, and SPT-3G DR1.
significance.value: 1.8σ (full-space) parameter difference from the CMB combination (Planck 2018, ACT-DR6, SPT-3G DR1); 2.6σ projected onto S8

summary.plain: Cosmology results from all six years of Dark Energy Survey data over about 5000 square degrees, combining 140 million galaxy shapes with galaxy clustering. The result sits 1.8σ from the CMB-based prediction in the full parameter space, and 2.6σ in the clustering amplitude alone.
summary.technical: DES Y6 3×2pt: S8 = 0.789 ± 0.012, Ωm = 0.333 (+0.023, -0.028) in ΛCDM, a (full-space) parameter difference of 1.8σ from Planck 2018 + ACT-DR6 + SPT-3G DR1 (2.6σ in S8 alone). wCDM: w = -1.12 (+0.26, -0.20). Combining all DES dark-energy probes (3×2pt, SNe Ia, BAO, clusters) gives a 2.8σ difference from the CMB.

title: Dark Energy Survey Year 6 Results: Cosmological Constraints from Galaxy Clustering and Weak Lensing
why_it_matters: The abstract states the DES Y6 constraints differ from a combination of CMB primary anisotropy datasets (Planck 2018, ACT-DR6, SPT-3G DR1) by 1.8σ in full parameter space and by 2.6σ projected onto S8.
